text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- President Suleyman Demirel will ask deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller to form the next government if Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigns so she can take a turn at the premiership.
- A British transport company, whose name is kept secret, will bid in a local transport tender in Istanbul.
MILLIYET
- Main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz says a government led by Ciller cannot win a vote of confidence in parliament.
- A court case investigating a security scandal over state ties with the underworld begins in Istanbul today.
HURRIYET
- The coalition partners announced at the weekend that they were going to call early elections within a year.
- The government will have to mint money to meet the cost of high subsidies given to farmers.
YENI YUZYIL
- Deputy Yasar Topcu, from the conservative main opposition party, said Ciller's husband had chaired the Turkish Intellengence Service when Ciller was prime minister.
- Entrepreneurs from the southeast return empty-handed from applying for subdidies promised by the Islamist-led government in a bid to develop the region.
RADIKAL

- President Demirel denies statements that the military criticed him for not taking the threat of Islamic fundamentalism seriously in his dealings with the Islamist-led government. But a high-ranking commander confirms the army was critical of Demirel.
DUNYA
- A tender for the building of a nuclear power plant is being postponed for two months.
- The Istanbul chambers of trade will invest to the eastern Black Sea region to fight high unemployment in the region.
ZAMAN
- The deputy chairman of the far-rightist Grand Unity Party says joining the current Islamist-led government for five months would be commiting suicide.
CUMHURIYET
- Turkish bridal gown maker Gagteks opens a branch in Russia.
